To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a deep learning paradigm for image feature extraction and analysis can be used to effectively detect CyanoHABs from images of inland water bodies acquired using a variety smartphones and uploaded on social media.
we have developed and tested a system to detect HABs from images acquired by smartphones.

(1) a deep learning approach can be used to extract features and classify images for HAB detection; (2) the proposed system can detect HABs with an accuracy of 90.6%; and (3) the system can detect HABS with an accuracy of up to 100% if the images have been pre-processed to enhance the cyanobacteria in the water.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following objectives: 1) Design of a deep learning paradigm for HAB detection using social media images of inland water bodies, 2) Development of a prototype system for automated detection of CyanoHABS using deep learning and 3) Demonstration of the proposed system on a set of images of inland water body acquired from OSM platforms.
the development of an early warning system for CyanoHABs based on the analysis of social media data and the design of a deep learning paradigm to detect HABs.

the following: (i) the use of deep learning for image feature extraction and HAB classification, (ii) the development of a cloud-based HAB detection and alerting system, (iii) the design and deployment of a smartphone app for image acquisition and transmission of HAB data and (iv) the development of an online portal for HAB detection and monitoring.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our system has the potential to be a powerful and cost effective tool for early detection of HABs and for rapid response to mitigate their harmful effects.
the current study is a first attempt at using social media data for the detection of CyanoHABS.
the proposed deep learning approach is a promising first step in the development of a comprehensive automated early detection, monitoring and warning system for CyanoHABs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose an automated deep learning paradigm for detection of CyanoHABS from social media images.
the proposed deep learning paradigm for the detection of harmful alga blooms is effective and can be used for early detection, warning, and rapid response systems.
the proposed approach is a promising solution that is scalable to large datasets and can be used for real-time HAB detection and early warning.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of deep learning approaches to feature extraction and classification can significantly improve the performance and robustness of HAB detection systems.
deep learning can be effectively used in the context of citizen science-based approaches in the area of environmental sustainability.
a deep learning paradigm is well suited for detection of HABs in images of inland water bodies acquired using a variety mobile devices.
